appraisal_events.evidence: il ne se suffisait plus à lui-même, il n'était plus que l'intermédiaire nécessaire entre ces jeunes filles et moi; le prestige que...son talent...ne valait plus qu'en tant qu'il m'en conférait un peu à moi-même aux yeux de la petite bande.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's earlier rapt admiration collapses into pure instrumental usefulness: Elstir's genius now matters only insofar as it can procure an introduction to the girls.

appraisal_events.evidence: Un étonnement provoqué par mes paroles précéda...l'air indifférent et distrait...'Tenez, passez-moi vite cette toile, me dit-il, j'entends Madame Elstir qui arrive...il est inutile que ma femme ait cette aquarelle sous les yeux.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Asked about the old portrait's model, Elstir is visibly startled, then affects indifference, minimizes the painting, and hastily conceals it before his wife arrives -- a furtive, evasive moment that undercuts his earlier transparent, masterly image.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'Ma belle Gabrielle !'...comme si rien que prononcer ces mots lui causait de l'attendrissement et de la vénération...il avait pu...le trouver méritoire, attendrissant, divin.
appraisal_events.explanation: Elstir addresses his wife with tender veneration, and the passage explains that he has come to see in her body the living incarnation of his lifelong artistic ideal, a devotion the narrator eventually comes to share.

status_effects.explanation: Elstir's standing in the narrator's eyes drops from admired genius to mere useful intermediary toward the desired girls.
A separate, later moment shows Elstir flustered and secretive about a past model, further chipping at the idealized portrait of him built up earlier in the visit.

Though the narrator first finds her dull and initially unlovely, Elstir's deep veneration -- and the narrator's own eventual understanding of it -- elevates her as the living embodiment of Elstir's artistic ideal.

ambiguities: The reference sheet resolves 'Miss Sacripant' to Odette, but within the passage itself this identity is not established: the narrator does not recognize the model and the connection functions as dramatic irony rather than an in-passage revelation, so the resulting appraisal movement (if any) toward Odette is left unmarked here.
'Madame Elstir' is not on the reference sheet; she is treated as a separate, unresolved named character introduced in this passage.
